thread.title: Research intelligence records
thread.preview:
I located the released copies of the **1-A contact sheet, letter, and envelope forms**, plus the **April 3, 2002 FBI communication**. The April 3 and April 16 communications repeat five paragraphs, so their connection claims trace to shared text. The September 2011 analyst email provides the strongest direct counterevidence on phone contact, but the released records do not let a reader reproduce the search. [FBI exhibits and the court’s document comparison, pp. 12–14](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Bulldog.pdf#page=12)

| Record | Findings and exact locators |
|---|---|
| **September 16, 2002 EC and 1-A enclosure** | S.D. Fla. **0:12-cv-61735-WJZ**, DE 25-2, PDF pp. 37–38, **SARASOTA-7–8**. FBI Tampa’s Fort Myers Resident Agency summarizes July 22 interviews and lists the enclosed contact-number photocopy and letter to an FDLE agent. FBI’s location index identifies the EC as **serial 2** and the enclosure as **[redacted case]-1A serial 1**. The FD-340 independently shows originating serial **2**, Tampa as the acquiring office, and **July 23, 2002** as the receipt date. The FD-340a shows **October 9, 2002** as the filing date. [EC, pp. 37–38](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf#page=37) · [Forms, DE 97-2, pp. 36–37, BULLDOG-38–39](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-97-2-Universe-of-Documents.pdf#page=36) · [FBI custody index, DE 97-3, pp. 3, 6](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-097-3-Index-Explaining-Location-of-Responsive-Records.pdf#page=3) |
| **Actual 1-A contents** | **BULLDOG-9**, PDF p. 10, is an undated handwritten contact sheet with redacted home, cell and fax entries. Its 2011 fax headers date transmissions of the copy. **BULLDOG-10–11**, pp. 11–12, is a letter dated **June 27, 2002** on its face, despite **June 17** in the FBI index. Its visible text discusses the return to Prestancia, vehicles, contact numbers, a planned sale and furniture removal to an unspecified destination. It reports no unusual gate activity in the context of that update. The full source numbers and physical envelope’s subsequent custody remain unverified. [Contact sheet and letter, DE 97-2, pp. 10–12](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-97-2-Universe-of-Documents.pdf#page=10) |
| **April 3 and April 16, 2002 ECs** | **April 3:** DE 97-2, pp. 72–74, **BULLDOG-74–76**, serial **1** in a redacted FBI file, recovered through ACS/Sentinel text search. Also reproduced in DE 72-1, pp. 7–9, and DE 99-1, Exhibit H, pp. 159–161. **April 16:** DE 25-2, pp. 35–36, **SARASOTA-5–6 / BULLDOG-5–6**, serial **1** in its indexed file. The visible language concerns connections to people or the investigation associated with the attacks. It leaves identities and supporting records obscured. **BULLDOG-36–37** is a separate pair of file-top records with April date references. The court left their creation date unclear. [April 3 EC](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-97-2-Universe-of-Documents.pdf#page=72) · [April 16 EC](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf#page=35) · [FBI index, pp. 3, 6, 10](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-097-3-Index-Explaining-Location-of-Responsive-Records.pdf#page=3) |
| **September 12, 2011 phone search** | **SARASOTA-33–35 / BULLDOG-33–35** preserves the **4:03 p.m.** Tampa analyst email, **4:51 p.m.** reply and **February 6, 2013** forward. The analyst reports searching available domestic family numbers in FBI and classified systems, including **three numbers beyond those in an FDLE report**, and finding no hijacker match. The FBI recovered the thread from the analyst’s email records. The analyst refers to an interview at **serial 3**, while the FBI index and FD-340 place the located September EC at **serial 2**. The redacted case identifiers prevent equating those references. The email does not establish which 1-A entries were used. [Email, DE 25-2, pp. 62–64](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf#page=62) · [FBI custody index, p. 6](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-097-3-Index-Explaining-Location-of-Responsive-Records.pdf#page=6) |
| **Director briefing and Review Commission source file** | **SARASOTA-1–2 / BULLDOG-1–2** was recovered among the Washington Field Office public affairs officer’s records. The page image confirms the heading **September 15, 2010**, even though it refers to the 2011 reporting. It also confirms **July 2002** for the interviews, correcting the starting chronology’s OCR concern. The Review Commission says it received a case-file copy, FOIA records and interview reports. Its principal Sarasota citation is the **April 30, 2014 MFR**, Broward Bulldog **1–4**, case **0:16-cv-61289-CMA**, DE 27-2 Ex. K pp. 37–40 and revised DE 68-1 Ex. G pp. 22–25. The court identifies duplicate Bates **221–224** and **702–705** and records the FBI’s declaration that it released **11 nonduplicative Sarasota case-file pages**. I located these docket references but did not recover the MFR exhibit pages or a complete inventory of what the Commission received. [Director briefing, pp. 31–32](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf#page=31) · [Commission report, printed pp. 105–107, nn. 356–359](https://www.fbi.gov/file-repository/reports-and-publications/final-9-11-review-commission-report-unclassified.pdf#page=106) · [Court order, DE 99](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/district-courts/florida/flsdce/0%3A2016cv61289/486466/99/) :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} |

The **strongest counterevidence** is the analyst’s first-person account of the negative comparison, supplemented by the director briefing’s report of a check against hijacker phones and calling cards. Their independence is unclear. The briefing also says the FBI *appears* not to have obtained the gate records, which limits its value as evidence against the alleged Atta and Jarrah entries. The strongest positive leads remain the contemporaneous FBI connection language and the specific reported gate and subpoena claims. The April ECs do not expose the comparisons behind those claims. The June 2002 letter’s gate observation concerns a later period, and the Commission’s account of the author’s inability to substantiate the EC comes through an FBI briefing. [Director briefing, p. 31](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf#page=31) · [Reported gate and phone claims, DE 99-1, p. 11](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-099-1-Declaration-of-Thomas-R.-Julin.pdf#page=11) · [Commission report, pp. 106–107](https://www.fbi.gov/file-repository/reports-and-publications/final-9-11-review-commission-report-unclassified.pdf#page=107)

**Unlocated:** The residence-line subpoena, carrier identity and certified returns, full 2011 input list, query logs and date ranges, hijacker comparison roster and output, gate sheets and plate images, and the Review Commission’s intake inventory. The FBI index does establish a separate Tampa PENTTBOM locator for the September 25 lead-coverage EC, **265D-NY-280350-TP, serial 4959, section 73 pp. 99–101**. That locator is for lead coverage, and the public index does not identify carrier returns there. [FBI location index, p. 5](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-097-3-Index-Explaining-Location-of-Responsive-Records.pdf#page=5)

**UMS / Max:** Searches of the visible exhibit text and public indexes found no authenticated company, worker, vehicle, phone or transaction match. The letter supplies a furniture-move lead but names neither a mover nor a destination in its visible text. Redacted identifiers and missing source records prevent a direct cross-match. [BULLDOG-11, PDF p. 12](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-97-2-Universe-of-Documents.pdf#page=12)

content.text: Please conduct deep research into the FBI Sarasota inquiry's underlying records, including SARASOTA-7–8's 1-A envelope (contact-information photocopies and letter), SARASOTA-33–35's September 12, 2011 analyst email, underlying phone-search inputs, queries, carrier returns, negative comparisons, and Review Commission source file and the April 3 and April 16, 2002 communications. Start with https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf and https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/main/investigation/broader-evidence/sarasota-gate-fbi-source-chronology-2026-11-11/README.md. Reconcile conflicting positive and negative accounts without assuming misconduct; differentiate document date markings from provenance and identify exact case, serial, Bates, exhibit and custodian locators. Search for authenticated UMS/Max links and report negative results and source limits. No outreach or requests. Provide original document links and pages, custody, strongest counterevidence and unlocated records.

content.text: Conduct deep research into the original CIA and FBI records behind the January 2000 al-Mihdhar intelligence hold and subsequent information-sharing. Locate and examine: (1) FBI detailee Dwight’s January 5 draft CIR, Michelle’s hold annotation, all versions and access, approval, release and dissemination logs; (2) Dwight’s January 13 follow-up email and attached draft, responses, and the February instruction to preserve the draft; (3) January 5 CIA cable SCALEC 134684, its routing and original evidence supporting or contradicting delivery of al-Mihdhar’s visa and travel documents to the FBI, including January 5–6 briefing records; and (4) the original July 13 and July 23, 2001 emails attributed to CIA officer John, responses, and evidence of actual dissemination. Use primary documents and archives, exact identifiers, dates, links and page locators. Distinguish original documents from later inspector-general summaries, court testimony substitutions, search snippets and secondary claims; report unsuccessful searches and access limits. Consider evidence supporting administrative or source-protection explanations as well as intentional withholding, without assuming either. Note any authenticated connection to UMS or the Saudi support network and explicitly distinguish missing evidence from negative findings. Do not submit FOIA requests or contact anyone. Produce a concise findings and missing-records table.

items.text:
**The public record supports an explicit hold on the draft CIR and its non-dissemination. It does not establish why it was held.** I located a released reproduction of the July 13 email; most requested January originals and audit records remain unlocated publicly.

Page numbers below are **printed report pages**, except where marked PDF.

| Record | Findings and source status | Missing records / limits |
|---|---|---|
| **January 5, 2000: Dwight’s draft CIR and Michelle’s annotation** | **Later investigative reconstruction, not the original.** DOJ OIG reports drafting around 9:30 a.m.; Michelle accessed it within an hour and entered the hold around 4 p.m. James and Eric accessed it January 5; Malcolm January 7. No recorded access by John to the draft. [DOJ report](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/archive/special/s0606/final.pdf), pp. 240–241. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} | Original CIR, stable document identifier, complete version history, annotation metadata, coordination/approval records and underlying access/release logs **not located**. Intended addressees do not establish receipt. |
| **January 13 follow-up and February preservation** | **CIA OIG summary:** January 13 Lotus Notes message attached the draft and asked John whether it should proceed or be revised; no reply found. Dwight accessed it February 11 and 16 and instructed a contractor to retain it while deleting other drafts. OIG recovered the **January 13 attachment version**. [CIA OIG C06184107](https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/cia/DOC_0006184107.pdf), p. 53, n. 13; PDF p. 78. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"} | Original message, attachment bytes, responses and preservation instructions unlocated. CIA OIG says CTC deleted its DUCS database during system retirement in late 2002; it could not date this draft’s individual deletion. That does **not establish selective destruction**. |
| **January 5: SCALEC 134684** | **Cable identified through OIG reporting; original not located.** It asserted that travel documents had reached FBI. CIA OIG could neither confirm nor refute delivery and found no subsequent receipt check. DOJ describes internal CIA distribution roughly three hours after the hold. CIA OIG pp. 54–55; DOJ pp. 242–243. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} | Full cable, exact routing, attachments, sender/recipient identities, transfer record and FBI acknowledgment. Its assertion is evidence **of a contemporaneous delivery claim**, not independently verified delivery. |
| **January 5–6 FBI briefing records** | DOJ describes a January 5 threat update incorporated into the January 6, 7:30 a.m. executive briefing, plus James’s briefing emails. These conveyed Malaysia information but omitted the visa. DOJ pp. 244–246. The Commission identifies **Rob → John et al., “Malaysia—for the record,” January 6, 2000**, in chapter 6, n. 50. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} | Standalone originals and complete recipient chains unlocated. These records support **partial information-sharing**, not passport/visa delivery. |
| **July 13, 2001 email** | **Released CIA document reproduction located:** **C05464169**, approved April 25, 2012, [PDF pp. 1–2](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/sites/default/files/documents/qx7xl1-j1w1s/2001-07-13-excised-khalad-excised-central.pdf). Visible text matches the reported opening and discussion of Khallad’s importance. The ending asks whether information can be sent, but its destination/method are redacted. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"} | Sender and routing are redacted. The archive labels it **“Richard to Alan”**; attribution to “John” therefore depends on later accounts, not visible sender metadata. Native email, full headers, recipient list and delivery logs remain unavailable. |
| **July 13 response; July 23 follow-up** | **Substituted testimony:** *United States v. Moussaoui*, **Defense Exhibit 939**, agreed March 11, 2006, [pp. 2–3](https://coop.vaed.uscourts.gov/moussaoui/exhibits/defense/939.pdf). It recounts a July 13 reply assigning Mary follow-up work, and July 23 renewed inquiry after no action. Thus, **“no response” is inaccurate for July 13**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"} | Original response and July 23 email unlocated. Exhibit 939 is neither an original email nor verbatim live testimony; its attached email concerns **August 24**, not July 23. |
| **Actual subsequent dissemination** | DOJ dates the CIR conveying the Khallad identification to **August 30, 2001**, distinguishing it from discovery of Mihdhar’s U.S. presence. DOJ pp. 298–299, 308. A separate [August 21 email reproduction](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/sites/default/files/documents/qx7xl1-j1w1s/2001-08-21-re-khalid-al-mihdhar-memorandum.pdf), p. 1, records an intention to send information to FBI. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"} | Original August 30 CIR and transmission/receipt logs unlocated. The August 21 intention is **not proof of completed delivery**. |

Administrative/source-protection explanations have some support: an officer later suggested the draft needed substantial editing to remove highly classified material and that staff believed documents had already been passed. CIA OIG explicitly presents this as **retrospective speculation**, not a contemporaneous explanation. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"} Conversely, the explicit hold and contradictory delivery claim warrant scrutiny. The Commission concluded contemporaneous documents contradicted the sharing claim; that does not independently establish a malicious motive. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}

**Search limits:** Exact-identifier, date and phrase searches across indexed CIA, DOJ, NARA, court and National Security Archive material did not yield the missing originals. NARA’s Master File is an archival lead, not an acquired document; its catalog returned no readable item-level content here. DOJ itself lacked independent CIA-database access. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="9"}

**Connections:** No examined record authenticated a UMS connection or linked these withholding decisions to Saudi support personnel. Bayoumi’s assistance to the same hijackers is separately documented; it does not establish that link. These are **unresolved evidentiary gaps, not findings disproving a connection**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}
